title: The ban on the National Syndicalists
summary: The Movimento Nacional-Sindicalista, founded in February 1932 by Francisco Rolão Preto and the nearest thing to a mass fascist movement Portugal produced, was dissolved by the government in 1934 and its leader sent out of the country; part of its membership was taken into the União Nacional and into the militia and youth organisations the regime built for itself. The blue shirts had wanted what the Estado Novo would not have — a single party with a street movement behind it, a leader rather than a president of the council, and a corporatism made from below. It is in the atlas because the suppression is where the difference between the Portuguese regime and the Italian one stops being a matter of interpretation: the Estado Novo destroyed its own fascists.
